descriptions.full:
A salon no-show policy that works, from Jordan Lee, owner of Northside Hair Studio, who took missed bookings from 14% to 4%. She shares which bookings get a deposit, the reminder text that lets clients cancel in seconds, and how her front desk handles late clients.

In this episode:
04:29 Deposits only on appointments over 90 minutes and first visits, not on every booking
17:12 Two reminders: 48 hours before, so the slot can be sold again, and the morning of the appointment
27:47 Late clients get 15 minutes, then choose a shorter service or a new time

episode_page.text:
# Salon No-Show Policy That Cut Missed Bookings to 4%

A salon no-show policy that works, from Jordan Lee, owner of Northside Hair Studio, who took missed bookings from 14% to 4%. She shares which bookings get a deposit, the reminder text that lets clients cancel in seconds, and how her front desk handles late clients.

## Listen
Apple Podcasts: [add link] | Spotify: [add link] | YouTube: [add link]

## Your guest
Jordan Lee owns Northside Hair Studio and runs a team of 6 stylists. She started as a stylist in 2009.

## Chapters
- 00:00 Why no-shows hurt a small salon
- 04:20 Deposits, a year later
- 17:05 Reminder texts that work
- 27:40 Handling late clients
- 35:10 One change to make this week
- 39:30 Where to find Jordan

## Key points
- 04:29 Deposits only on appointments over 90 minutes and first visits, not on every booking
- 17:12 Two reminders: 48 hours before, so the slot can be sold again, and the morning of the appointment
- 27:47 Late clients get 15 minutes, then choose a shorter service or a new time

## In their words
> "We were losing about 14% of booked appointments, and on a color booking that is a three hour hole in the day." (Jordan Lee, 01:42)
> "The biggest change is that we stopped taking a deposit on every booking. Now it's only appointments over 90 minutes and first visits." (Jordan Lee, 04:29)
> "With the deposits and the new reminders together, we're down to 4% from 14%." (Jordan Lee, 25:10)
> "Send the reminder 48 hours out instead of 24, and let people cancel by text. That alone moved us from 14% to 9%." (Jordan Lee, 35:17)
